hero.title: Real-Time Indexing: How Google Indexes Content in Minutes, Not Days
hero.subtitle: Google maintains a three-tier crawl architecture (Base 200M+, Daily 50M+, Real-time 5M+) that enables near-instant indexing for high-priority URLs. Chrome browser signals feed directly into ranking through CRAPS (Chrome Realtime Aggregated Page Signals), while InstantGlue delivers user engagement data with ~10-minute latency. The API leak revealed RealTimeBoost, a re-ranking twiddler that incorporates live Chrome visit data, and a family of CRAPS signals that recompute site quality (NSR) and URL-level freshness in real time.

keyInsight.label: Key Insight from API Leak + Patents
keyInsight.text: Google's real-time indexing is not just about crawling faster. The API leak reveals a dual pipeline: Trawler's three-tier crawl scheduler (Patent US7725452) determines how quickly content is fetched, while CRAPS signals (crapsNewUrlSignals, crapsAbsoluteHostSignals) determine how quickly it influences rankings. The RealTimeBoost twiddler bridges both pipelines, re-ranking results using incoming Chrome visits before the traditional NavBoost table is updated. For high-engagement URLs, the gap between publishing and ranking impact can be as short as 10 minutes via InstantGlue.

pillars.title: API Leak Signals
items: RealTimeBoost - Re-ranking twiddler incorporating real-time signals including incoming Chrome visits. Applied as a post-retrieval boost for content receiving sudden engagement spikes before the full NavBoost pipeline processes the data

crapsNewUrlSignals - Chrome Realtime Aggregated Page Signals for new/fresh URLs. Provides immediate engagement metrics for recently discovered pages that lack historical NavBoost data, solving the cold-start problem for fresh content

crapsAbsoluteHostSignals - Chrome Realtime Aggregated Page Signals at the host level. Aggregates Chrome browsing behavior across an entire domain, providing real-time site-level quality signals that can influence all pages on that host

crapsNewNsrSignal - Site-level NSR (Normalized Site Rank) recomputed using CRAPS data in near-real-time. Allows site quality scores to update rapidly when Chrome engagement patterns shift, rather than waiting for the next batch NSR computation

pillars.title: 4 Patents
items: Patent US20060294086: Realtime Indexing in Rapidly Changing Document Collections - Foundational patent for real-time indexing. Describes maintaining a real-time index partition that is continuously updated as documents change, merged periodically with the main index. Enables sub-second indexing latency for the highest-priority content tier

Patent US7634466: Realtime Indexing - Near-real-time indexing system for rapidly changing content. Implements incremental index updates without requiring full index rebuilds. The real-time partition handles insertions, deletions, and modifications as a streaming operation

Patent US7725452: Scheduler for Search Engine Crawler - Three-tier crawl architecture: Base (200M+ URLs, comprehensive coverage), Daily (50M+ URLs, frequent changers), Real-time (5M+ URLs, breaking/critical content). Priority scoring combines PageRank, change frequency, and content importance to route URLs into the appropriate tier

Patent US8458163: Website Owner Crawl Rate Management - Allows site owners to request faster or slower crawl rates via Search Console. Speed-up requests are only honored when the current rate limit is the binding constraint: |currentLimit - maxActualRate| < threshold. If the crawler is already below server capacity, a speed-up request has no effect

pillars.title: Real-Time Indexing Implications
items: Chrome traffic is a real-time ranking input, not just a passive signal: CRAPS signals (crapsNewUrlSignals, crapsAbsoluteHostSignals) mean Chrome browsing data feeds ranking in near-real-time. If your content receives a surge of Chrome visits (from social media, email newsletters, direct shares), RealTimeBoost can amplify your ranking before the regular NavBoost cycle processes the data. This creates a flywheel: early traffic generates real-time signals that boost rankings, driving more traffic

New URLs have a dedicated real-time signal path: crapsNewUrlSignals specifically addresses fresh URLs, solving the cold-start problem. When you publish new content and it receives immediate Chrome engagement, the system does not wait for historical NavBoost data to accumulate. This means early promotion of new content (via email lists, social channels, push notifications) directly feeds the real-time ranking pipeline

Site-level CRAPS signals affect all your pages: crapsAbsoluteHostSignals operates at the domain level. If your site as a whole receives strong Chrome engagement, all pages benefit from the real-time host-level signal. Conversely, a sudden drop in site-wide Chrome engagement (site outage, bad press, migration issues) can depress rankings across all pages in near-real-time

The three-tier crawl determines your content's indexing speed ceiling: Only ~5M URLs qualify for real-time crawl. To reach this tier, content needs high PageRank, demonstrated change frequency, and content importance signals. Most sites operate in the Daily (50M+) or Base (200M+) tiers. Improving server response time, internal linking to new content, and maintaining consistent update cadence are prerequisites for faster crawl tier assignment

Search Console crawl rate requests have strict conditions: Patent US8458163 reveals that speed-up requests only work when the current crawl rate limit is actually the bottleneck. If your server is slow or content quality is low, requesting faster crawling has zero effect. Fix server performance first, then request rate increases

NSR recomputation via CRAPS means site reputation can shift rapidly: crapsNewNsrSignal recalculates your site's Normalized Site Rank using real-time Chrome data. A viral positive event (featured in major media, trending product launch) can improve your NSR within hours rather than waiting for the next batch computation. The reverse is also true: a brand crisis visible in Chrome traffic patterns can depress NSR quickly

pillars.title: System Context
items: Crawl scale as competitive advantage - Judge Mehta's opinion identifies Google's crawl infrastructure and index scale as structural competitive advantages. The ability to crawl 200M+ URLs in the base tier alone, with 5M+ in real-time, requires infrastructure investment that constitutes a barrier to entry for competitors

Elizabeth Reid on crawl scheduling - 'Index tiering and crawl scheduling are among Google's most sensitive proprietary assets.' The three-tier crawl architecture and the criteria for real-time tier assignment are classified as trade secrets

Chrome data feeds ranking - DOJ trial testimony confirmed Chrome browsing data as a ranking input. The CRAPS signal family in the API leak provides the technical mechanism: Chrome visits are aggregated in real time and fed into ranking signals at both URL and host levels

Note: No specific DOJ exhibits target real-time indexing mechanisms directly. The above references are drawn from Judge Mehta's opinion on Google's infrastructure advantages and general trial testimony about Chrome data usage in ranking

calculations.name: Real-Time Crawl Tier Assignment
calculations.how: The crawler scheduler assigns each URL to one of three crawl tiers based on a composite priority score. The score combines PageRank (link-based importance), content change frequency (detected by comparing checksums across successive crawls), and content importance (predicted query utility). URLs in the Real-time tier (top ~5M) are fetched within minutes of a change being detected or signaled. Daily-tier URLs (~50M) are recrawled every 24 hours. Base-tier URLs (~200M+) follow a longer cycle based on their individual priority scores.
calculations.formula: CrawlTier(url) = if priority(url) >= T_realtime: Real-time (~5M URLs) if priority(url) >= T_daily: Daily (~50M URLs) else: Base (~200M+ URLs) priority(url) = f( PageRank(url), changeFrequency(checksum_history), contentImportance(predicted_query_utility) ) // Real-time: fetched within minutes // Daily: recrawled every ~24h // Base: recrawled on longer cycles
calculations.affects: Affected by: PageRank, content change rate, predicted query utility, server response speed, sitemap signals

calculations.name: RealTimeBoost Signal Computation
calculations.how: RealTimeBoost operates as a post-retrieval re-ranking twiddler that incorporates real-time Chrome visit data. When a URL receives a sudden spike in Chrome visits (detected via CRAPS aggregation), RealTimeBoost applies a positive re-ranking signal before the standard NavBoost table is updated. The signal combines crapsNewUrlSignals (URL-level Chrome engagement for fresh URLs) with crapsAbsoluteHostSignals (host-level Chrome engagement). For new URLs without NavBoost history, crapsNewUrlSignals provides the primary engagement signal, solving the cold-start problem.
calculations.formula: RealTimeBoost(url, query) = twiddler( crapsNewUrlSignals(url), crapsAbsoluteHostSignals(host), chromeVisitSpike(url, window) ) // Applied post-retrieval, before final ranking // Bridges gap between publish and NavBoost update for new URLs: engagement = crapsNewUrlSignals(url) // cold-start bypass: no NavBoost history needed for all URLs: siteBoost = crapsAbsoluteHostSignals(host) // host-level Chrome engagement lifts all pages
calculations.affects: Affected by: Chrome visit volume and velocity, CRAPS signal freshness, host-level engagement patterns, NavBoost data availability

calculations.name: Real-Time NSR Recomputation
calculations.how: Normalized Site Rank (NSR) is normally computed in batch cycles, but crapsNewNsrSignal enables near-real-time recomputation using Chrome browsing data. When aggregate Chrome engagement patterns for a host shift significantly (viral event, site outage, brand crisis), the NSR is recomputed without waiting for the next batch cycle. This updated NSR then influences all ranking decisions for pages on that host, including index tier placement and crawl priority.
calculations.formula: crapsNewNsrSignal(host) = recompute( NSR(host), crapsAbsoluteHostSignals(host) ) // Triggers on significant Chrome engagement shift // Bypasses standard batch NSR computation cycle impact(host) = crapsNewNsrSignal → { crawlPriority, indexTierPlacement, rankingCeiling } // All pages on host affected by NSR update
calculations.affects: Affected by: aggregate Chrome browsing patterns at host level, engagement velocity changes, site-wide traffic trends

stages.name: Change Detection
stages.detail: URL change detected via sitemap ping, RSS feed, Google Alerts, or checksum difference on recrawl

stages.name: Crawl Tier Routing
stages.detail: Scheduler assigns URL to Real-time (5M+), Daily (50M+), or Base (200M+) tier based on priority score

stages.name: Real-Time Fetch
stages.detail: Trawler fetches Real-time tier URLs within minutes. Content rendered and parsed for indexing

stages.name: Real-Time Index Partition
stages.detail: New/updated content enters the real-time index partition (Patent US20060294086). Merged periodically with main index

stages.name: CRAPS Signal Aggregation
stages.detail: Chrome Realtime Aggregated Page Signals computed: crapsNewUrlSignals (URL-level), crapsAbsoluteHostSignals (host-level)

stages.name: RealTimeBoost Application
stages.detail: Post-retrieval twiddler applies real-time Chrome engagement data to re-rank results before NavBoost table update

stages.name: InstantGlue Delivery
stages.detail: User engagement signals delivered with ~10-minute latency on 24h windows. Feeds isHotdoc flag for trending content

timeline.title: Realtime Indexing Patent Filed
timeline.desc: US20060294086 filed: describes maintaining a real-time index partition continuously updated as documents change.

timeline.title: Crawl Scheduler Patent
timeline.desc: US7725452 granted: three-tier crawl architecture (Base 200M+, Daily 50M+, Real-time 5M+) for prioritized crawling.

timeline.title: Realtime Indexing Granted
timeline.desc: US7634466 granted: near-real-time incremental index updates without full index rebuilds.

timeline.title: Caffeine Launch
timeline.desc: Google replaces batch indexing with continuous incremental indexing. Content can enter the index within seconds of crawling.

timeline.title: Crawl Rate Management Patent
timeline.desc: US8458163 granted: site owners can request crawl rate changes, but speed-up only honored when rate limit is the binding constraint.

timeline.title: API Leak Reveals CRAPS + RealTimeBoost
timeline.desc: RealTimeBoost, crapsNewUrlSignals, crapsAbsoluteHostSignals, and crapsNewNsrSignal exposed. Chrome real-time signal pipeline confirmed.

timeline.title: Mehta Opinion on Infrastructure
timeline.desc: Judge Mehta identifies Google's crawl scale and Chrome data integration as structural competitive advantages constituting barriers to entry.

contradictions.publicClaim: It can take time for Google to discover and index new content. Indexing can take anywhere from a few days to a few weeks.
contradictions.internalClaim: Chrome Realtime Aggregated Page Signals provide near-real-time engagement data for new URLs. RealTimeBoost re-ranks results using live Chrome visits. For high-engagement URLs, the gap between publishing and ranking impact can be as short as 10 minutes via InstantGlue.

contradictions.publicClaim: There's no way to guarantee that Google will index your content faster. Submitting a sitemap or using the URL Inspection tool can help but doesn't guarantee faster indexing.
contradictions.internalSource: Patent US7725452 + API Leak CRAPS signals
contradictions.internalClaim: The three-tier crawl architecture routes ~5M URLs into a real-time crawl tier with minutes-level fetch latency. URLs that demonstrate high PageRank, content importance, and change frequency are automatically promoted to faster crawl tiers. Chrome engagement data (CRAPS) further accelerates ranking impact for content receiving real-time traffic.

contradictions.publicClaim: We don't use Chrome data for ranking. Chrome usage data is not used in Search ranking.
contradictions.internalClaim: CRAPS literally stands for Chrome Realtime Aggregated Page Signals. Three distinct CRAPS signals feed ranking: URL-level (crapsNewUrlSignals), host-level (crapsAbsoluteHostSignals), and NSR recomputation (crapsNewNsrSignal). RealTimeBoost incorporates Chrome visits as a re-ranking twiddler.
